question: Under India's National Immunization Schedule (NIS), which of the following vaccine combinations is correctly given at 6 weeks of age?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: BCG, OPV0 and Hepatitis B are given at birth, not at 6 weeks.
Correct. The NIS schedules Pentavalent (DTP-HepB-Hib), OPV, Rotavirus, and fIPV (fractional IPV) at 6 weeks, 10 weeks, and 14 weeks.
MR, JE (live), and PCV are given at 9–12 months, not at 6 weeks.
DPT and OPV boosters are given at 16–24 months (first booster) and 5–6 years (second booster).

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the NIS schedule: birth vaccines (BCG/OPV0/HepB), 6/10/14-week vaccines (Penta/OPV/Rota/fIPV), and 9–12-month vaccines (MR/JE/PCV).
At 6, 10, and 14 weeks the NIS gives Pentavalent + OPV + Rotavirus + fIPV — the core primary series.
